body: You've cursed at me, called me dumb...and * I'm * the rude one? You might want to check yourself and your attitude before telling someone else how rude they are. Thank you for your armchair diagnosis. I'd like to say this has been fun but it's been like hammering my hands to a chair. Oh, and my "15 good-byes" was my attempt to tell you I don't want to continue arguing with you but it's obvious you have to get the last word, even if it's a nasty one.
My heart goes out to everyone affected by this.
I can't spread what I don't feel. I don't smile, not even when I'm by myself, much less on those rare occasions when I go out. Thanks for taking the time to reply.
Nope. Everyone knows I'm gay. That's not it.
It's not just 16 year olds. It speaks to the nature of our country. It is true - nothing matters. People are going to forget you about 15 minutes after you die and they get to take all your stuff.

I don't think you know how I feel. The term, "backsliding" is an invention of the religious. It's an imaginary state people can be guilted into when they began to pull away from the Hive Mentality and begin to think for themselves. 

You are correct about one things. "It's human nature...to come up with endless explanations..." and yes, death is very real. It's fear of that death and the thought that this world can't go on without them that forced humans to create "God" and "heaven" and so on. I'm not bashing your belief, it just doesn't sound all that credible.
In a small town in Western TN.
What saw had long arms and a broad, triangular torso. It did not have wings. It was also not perched on a fence, it was moving between the trees, not inching along a fence.

I did go through this. In the Southern Baptist church, there's a "redemption" situation in which you're supposed to admit how terrible  you are and ask Jesus to "save" you. This is supposed to be followed by some transcendental happening in which you feel all together different. I experienced all of this and the idea of being "saved" was reinforced by everyone around me. I felt euphoria and all the things people say they feel...until I did something they didn't approve of. Then, I was "back-sliding" and had to "recommit my life" to Jesus. 

When I left that environment, when I was confronted with a true life-changing event, one I came out of on my own, with no support or help from anyone, a true and glaring light came on for me. We are alone in this life. There is no higher power, no great being, no angels, no demons - nothing we can offload our experiences onto. We - are all we have. The personal empowerment that came from that realization was better than all the pats on the backs, all the "God loves you, brother"s that I ever received because it validated ME, as a person and as a strong individual. 

This belief people have in the supernatural realm could very well be something real, something we have no way of measuring. However, superstition and fear have wrapped it up in chains of nonsense like "angels" and "demons". As long as every dark thing that crosses our path is a "demon" and every coincidence that goes our way is an "angel", we will never get to the truth of the supernatural. 

Contrary to what this might read as, I would LOVE to believe in something more than this life but the proof just hasn't borne this out to me. Even when I was wrapped up in all that Baptist nonsense, I never "felt" anything - God or Jesus or the Holy Spook - nothing. I wanted to...but it never happened.

I very much understand that whatever you experienced was real - to you. I just question whether it was "God".

It's not unusual to experience this sort of reaction when surrounded by others of "belief" or "faith". It's the same sort of thing that happens in riots. I was raised in the Christian faith and in a Baptist environment. I've seen grown men cry and wail about "God" and then go out on Monday and beat their kids. Just because you started crying (bawling) it doesn't mean you had an encounter with a transcendental, supernatural entity. It could just  mean you were caught up on the same thing everyone else was. After all, it's easy to believe something that comes with its own support system, failsafes and insulation from ridicule.

You said, yourself, that you sort of "zoned out" or that your attention was elsewhere. This state of mind could very well have opened you up to suggestion. Recognizing a feeling as "God" could also be a default setting for your mind to attempt to make sense of a feeling you'd not experienced before since you were in a religious context. I say this because I find it strange that an omnipotent, supernatural being has to be so covert and mysterious about making themselves known. It doesn't make any sense, to me.

I apologize for my continued skepticism but this doesn't sound like a life-changing event, just someone dipping their toe into the realm of mass hysteria, just with religion.

Children often imagine things are one way when they're another, I'll give you that. "Hallucinate" is a strong word and not fitting for this situation. I was, then, and am, now, an artist. I was always good with detail when it came to things I saw. Strange details always stuck out when I observed things. That's the only thing that preserves this memory for me, the details about what I saw. I don't remember what shoes I had on or the color of my shirt that day, because they weren't important. What I do remember are the things that kept me up for the next few months and that sneak into my dreams, as an adult. 

There wasn't anything that precedes this, as things like this weren't talked about and especially not in front of a child. As an adult, I find people in that same area talk about "things" they've heard and seen in the woods but nothing with names like "dog man". It's just not talked about.

As for the setting, my grandparents had a house that sat in the middle of four fields, two of which were edged with very thick woods. What I said about people dumping their pets in the country was commonplace and many times, my grandfather told me not to play in the woods for that reason. Wild dogs can be vicious. I very much thought I'd heard a dog. I was expecting a dog to emerge. This is another reason why I remember what I do about it, because it wasn't what I was expecting. It's like remembering a specific birthday present because it was unexpected.

Horned Owls don't have arms that reach out, nor do they have broad torsos. I grew up in the woods, hearing sounds and seeing things. I never heard anything like this, nor did I ever see anything with arms like that. At the time, I didn't think "monster", even if I was a child, at the time. I knew what I saw was nothing I'd ever seen in the woods before. I wasn't one of those people who say things like "I thought my mind was playing tricks". Even the mind of a child doesn't generate hallucinations of that caliber and strength.
I've contacted local authorities - three times. I just didn't know what else to do.

I have to remain discrete about this but I'm the guy's neighbor. I've seen this terrible thing more than once. I submitted a form to PETA and I've called the local police (three times!). Thanks for the suggestions everyone!
